For what benefit from this anymore, if nothing is upon us, yet rather our things have been hung upon others? And somehow equal and similar hereafter, to those knowing the nomoi / laws, also the one having been ignorant of them, if it does not belong to those willing to do freely whatever they should perhaps choose; yet I say the guides of the nomoi / laws have become most unjust, although having chosen upon themselves as much glory of justice as possible. For they have legislated—I do not know how—that the careless must be punished, and pay bitter justices of the transgression, and they have handed over as it were canons to the young and most praiseworthy manners of pedagogy, either as being upon us ourselves to choose to live through solemnly, or I do not know what having thought. And someone would say, I think: Well, O Solon, you were legislating for those then; yet it was somehow altogether necessary to persuade Heimarmenē / Fate besides to grant to those being legislated whatever they should wish to think and do.
